confounds: The corpus contains substantial canned greetings, promotional material, and platform-generated profile-view notices; these can distort lexical and repetition statistics.
Labels are highly imbalanced: 618 diagnosed users versus 5,463 controls, so prevalence calibration should not be inferred from raw class proportions.
Pronoun, tense, connective, quotation, and humor detection uses simple Portuguese surface lexicons with polysemy and morphology errors.
Age, gender, education, dialect, social network, posting genre, and platform conventions may explain stylistic differences.
The diagnosed/control labels are outcomes to explain; none of these signals establishes causality, depression status, or clinical diagnostic validity.

caveats: Counts use surface pronoun heuristics and include possessives.
Quote, lyric, joke, advocacy, and third-person contexts cannot be perfectly separated with surface rules.
findings.evidence_summary: The effect was consistent across all folds, with fold AUCs about 0.686–0.716. Plural first-person reference was not elevated, suggesting the signal is specifically singular self-reference rather than collective language.
findings.prompt_guidance: Use singular self-reference as a contextual stylistic feature, preferably combined with nearby predicates and message form; do not treat pronoun presence as clinical evidence.

quantitative_support.measure: Median user-level share of posts containing first-person singular reference
Self-reference share after excluding heuristic joke/quote/news-like posts

findings.signal: First-person singular self-reference is the strongest low-level divergence.

caveats: These are form-based combinations, not validated indicators of subjective experience.
Question marks may reflect outward dialogue, quotation, or rhetorical style.
findings.evidence_summary: All three combinations retained the same direction in every development fold, outperforming the corresponding isolated low-level markers in several cases.
findings.prompt_guidance: Prefer interaction features such as self-reference plus negation/question/length over isolated keyword counts.

quantitative_support.measure: Median share of posts containing both self-reference and negation
Median share of posts containing both self-reference and a question mark
Median share of posts containing self-reference and at least 20 tokens

findings.signal: Self-reference is more informative when combined with negation, questions, or longer messages.

caveats: Connective words are polysemous and do not measure formal syntax directly.
Message genre, education, age, and platform conventions may affect length.
findings.evidence_summary: The direction was stable across all folds. Sentence length remained higher in a fixed 50-post window, reducing dependence on total timeline size; multi-sentence frequency itself was not different.
findings.prompt_guidance: Use length and connective markers as weak syntactic-complexity proxies, preferably normalized by a fixed post window.
findings.signal: Diagnosed users produce modestly longer messages and sentence units, with slightly more connective-marker usage.

caveats: Questions may be conversational, rhetorical, quoted, or engagement-seeking.
The effect is small and should not be interpreted clinically.
findings.evidence_summary: The effect was positive in every fold and persisted in a fixed 50-post window, indicating it is not explained solely by more retained posts.
findings.prompt_guidance: Use question-post prevalence rather than raw question counts, and combine it with self-reference or message length.

quantitative_support.measure: Median user-level share of posts containing a question mark
Question-post prevalence in the first 50 posts

findings.signal: Question use is modestly higher among diagnosed users.

caveats: Joke/laughter detection is surface-based and can miss or misclassify humor.
Demographics, conversational networks, and platform norms are plausible explanations.
findings.evidence_summary: Both measures favored controls in all four folds; this contrasts with the higher question rate and suggests a specific punctuation/register difference rather than generally more punctuation.
findings.prompt_guidance: Treat lower exclamation or laughter-marker rates as weak supporting features only, with genre controls.

quantitative_support.measure: Median user-level share of posts containing exclamation marks

findings.signal: Controls show more exclamatory and laughter-like surface style.

caveats: Repeated greetings, automated text, and promotional templates can create this pattern.
Do not equate recurrence with cognitive rigidity or clinical symptoms.
findings.evidence_summary: Repeated two-token openings favored diagnosed users in every fold, whereas exact duplicate posts were indistinguishable. The signal is weak and partly activity-sensitive.
findings.prompt_guidance: Use recurring opening structures only after controlling for timeline length and common boilerplate.

quantitative_support.measure: Median share of posts with a repeated two-token opening

findings.signal: Repeated post openings are modestly higher, but exact copy-paste repetition is not.

caveats: Differences may reflect activity, retention duration, collection rules, or demographic composition rather than label-related style.
findings.evidence_summary: The volume direction was stable across folds. Fixed-window analyses showed that the main self-reference and sentence-length effects persist, but aggregate vocabulary and repetition measures are strongly volume-sensitive.
findings.prompt_guidance: Prefer per-user rates, fixed windows, or explicit volume adjustment; never use pooled post frequency as user evidence.
findings.signal: Diagnosed timelines are modestly more prolific, making volume a material confound.

negative_results: Equal-length lexical diversity was null: random 500-token TTR was 0.592 diagnosed versus 0.588 control (AUC 0.515); top-10 vocabulary share was also equal.
Exact duplicate-post rate, overall punctuation density, comma use, semicolon use, and multi-sentence rate showed no reliable separation.
Token-normalized negation was null (2.56 versus 2.55 per 100 tokens; AUC 0.492); second-person pronouns were also null.
Tense proxies were weak and heuristic: future-post prevalence was only slightly higher in diagnosed users, while past-marker frequency was slightly lower.
